summary: The app's own sketch solver now names more of the problems PlaneGCS names, so feedback no longer depends on PlaneGCS for them. A sketch whose dimensions cannot agree, and whose solve stalls short of the collapsed point nearest to meeting them, was only suspected before, with no relation named. Native now also diagnoses it where it started, as PlaneGCS does, and keeps the dependencies found there only between relations that are the same function of the same values, as repeated dimensions are, since those depend on each other wherever the sketch moves; when one of them disagrees, the sketch is blamed for them: distances of 10, 12 and 14 between two points 20 apart vertically now name the three distances, as PlaneGCS does. Other dependencies a start shows can be accidents of where it begins, as a point held by symmetry on the line between two centres it must be 5 from, so they are not blamed, and a sketch with no disagreeing repeat stays suspected. A solved sketch with a group whose diagnosis ran out of work was rejected as not diagnosable and lost every label; now that group labels nothing and leaves freedom unknown, while the other groups are still diagnosed. An exact copy of a relation whose dependence was too close to call, as one beside a near tangency, is now found redundant or conflicting instead of left unlabelled. While PlaneGCS is still bundled, the app asks it first for blame from a stalled start and for sketches not wholly diagnosed, and keeps the native answer only when PlaneGCS neither solves nor names conflicts or redundancies, so its answers are unchanged where PlaneGCS answers. Across the full test suite, the only solves whose rank was too close to call, other than drags, were nine on a tangency with nothing free, so such solves still skip the move toward the solution nearest their start.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. The native solver module and the app now speak buffer protocol 5, which adds the diagnosis kinds from-start and incomplete; they ship together and nothing stores the protocol. With PlaneGCS bundled, sketches answer as before unless PlaneGCS neither solves nor names conflicts or redundancies for a stalled sketch blamed from its start, which now names the conflicts the start shows instead of failing without ids, or for a solved sketch with a group not diagnosed, which is now solved with freedom unknown instead of rejected. The native-only mode answers both. A repeated dimension beside a near tangency may now be named redundant or conflicting where it was not. Solve records name the new fallback reasons start-diagnosis and incomplete.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage, journal or worker reply schema change. The native solver's buffer protocol moves from 4 to 5 with two diagnosis kinds; the module and its reader ship together. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. Solve records gain the fallback reasons start-diagnosis and incomplete.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and result fields.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Rust tests blame distances of 10, 12 and 14 with a vertical offset of 20 as their start shows, [C, C, C, 0], with the 12 given between the points the other way round, and with a repeated 10 and the offset negated between the points the other way round both redundant, keeping the values where the solve stopped; the same sketch dragged stays suspected; a point starting by accident on the line between two centres it must be 5 from solves alone, and joined to such a conflict only the conflict is blamed, wherever it starts; a satisfiable sketch held on a saddle, where its start shows two distances dependent, stays suspected; a stalled conflict beside a nearly vertical line through the point blames only the conflicting dimensions; beside a suspected triangle the sketch stays suspected and beside a near tangency it is blamed from the start, each group keeping its labels; over every work limit from 0 to 8,000 the diagnosis only moves from unavailable to suspected to blamed from the start. A group that runs out of work while diagnosed is incomplete, with the other group still labelled, and one that did not converge stays unavailable. An exact copy of an undecided row, or its negation, is found with that row alone and agrees as its residuals do, while a copy one ulp off is not. The runtime tests take PlaneGCS's answer for blame from the start and for incomplete sketches when it solves, return native's own conflicts or solution with freedom unknown when PlaneGCS fails or throws, and answer in native-only mode without loading PlaneGCS; the reader accepts the new kinds and rejects blame from the start for a converged sketch. The workload benchmark names PlaneGCS's three overlapping conflicts in native-only mode, and pins PlaneGCS on the overlapping conflicts with a repeated 10, which native names redundant where PlaneGCS names it conflicting. The native differential suites keep their four reviewed differences. All Rust suites, the sketch-solver and benchmark Vitest suites, and the full test suite pass.

publicNotes.summary: The app's own sketch solver names more conflicting and redundant relations itself.
changes: Names the conflicting dimensions of a sketch whose solve stalls short of meeting them, as the start shows, where it named none before when PlaneGCS could not answer.
Solves a sketch with freedom unknown when one part of it is too costly to diagnose, instead of rejecting it, while still naming problems in the other parts.
Finds a repeated relation beside a near tangency as redundant or conflicting.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
